analysis.investment_thesis: Indigo Paints is a credible challenger brand in a large Indian decorative paints market, but the FY25 growth stall — revenue up just 2.7% and net profit down 4.7% YoY — signals the fast-grower story is on pause, not accelerating. At a PEG of ~1.4 based on a decelerating earnings profile, the price doesn't compensate for execution risk.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage (D/E: 0.02) with 19.5% ROCE — capital-light model generating real returns
OCF surged to INR 206 Cr in FY25 (+36% YoY), showing operating quality improving even as profits dipped
Differentiated product portfolio (leakproof, roof, tile paints) carves defensible niches vs. Asian Paints/Berger giants
key_risks: Growth deceleration is the biggest red flag — revenue CAGR was 14.2% but FY25 growth collapsed to ~2.7%; net profit fell 149→142 Cr
EBITDA margins contracted from 18.3% (FY24) to 17.5% (FY25) — exactly what Lynch hates: revenue growing but profit shrinking
CWIP exploded from INR 17 Cr to 221 Cr in FY25 — heavy capex cycle ahead could pressure FCF and test execution
red_flags: FY25 net profit declined YoY (149→142 Cr) — the story is weakening, not strengthening
Revenue near-stalled at 2.7% growth in FY25 — for a stock priced at P/E 26.9x, this is a mismatch
Finance costs growing at 44% CAGR (1→4 Cr) — minor now but signals balance sheet shift
analysis.detailed_analysis:
As Peter Lynch, I'd classify Indigo Paints as a wannabe fast-grower that's hit a speed bump. The 3-year earnings CAGR of 19.1% gives a PEG of ~1.41 — already above my comfort zone of 1.0 — and that historical number flatters what's actually happening now. FY25 tells a worrying story: revenue barely moved (+2.7%), earnings fell, and EBITDA margins compressed 80 bps. When a supposed growth stock stops growing, the P/E of 26.9x becomes very uncomfortable. I'd need to see the growth story reignite before getting excited.

The balance sheet is genuinely clean — 0.02 D/E is almost as good as it gets, and OCF of INR 206 Cr with FCF turning positive is encouraging. The brand has real differentiation in a INR 75,000+ Cr market dominated by Asian Paints. But the CWIP jump from INR 17 Cr to 221 Cr tells me they're plowing capital into a new capacity wave — that's a bet on future growth that must be proved out. Until FY26 numbers show revenue back above 15% growth and margins recovering, this sits in my "wait and watch" pile, not my buy list.
